title: Yi Jianlian

{{Chinese name|Yi}}
'''Yi Jianlian''' ([[Traditional Chinese]]: 易建聯, [[Simplified Chinese]]: 易建联, [[Standard Cantonese|Cantonese]]: '''Yik Kin Luen''' [[Pinyin]]: ''Yì Jiànlián''), officially born on [[October 27]], [[1987]] (this has been questioned; see [[#Age discrepancy|below]]), in [[Shenzhen]], [[Guangdong]] is a [[China|Chinese]] [[basketball]] player.  He plays for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of 
the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].

He is 2.14 meters, or 7’0” tall and weighing 112 kilograms (220 pounds).
==Career==
===Pre-NBA Career===
Yi’s father is 1.99 meters (6’6”) tall, his mother is 1.72 meters (5’8”) and both of them were retired professional handball players.<ref name="ref1">{{cite news
  | first= Li
  | last=  Xiao
  | author=
  | url= http://www.china.org.cn/english/2003/Sep/75681.htm
  | title= Little Giant Yi Jianlian: I Want to Play NBA Basketball
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[September 22]], [[2003]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-02
}}</ref> Yi started playing basketball when he was 12,<ref name="ref2">{{cite news
  | first= 
  | last=  
  | author=
  | url= http://espn.go.com/recruiting/s/2002/0709/1403721.html
  | title= Yi no Yao, but ABCD has Chinese flavor
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[July 9]], [[2002]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-25
}}</ref> was 1.93 meters (6’3”) by the time he was 13, and could already touch 3.51 meters (6'11”) by the time he joined the Guangdong Tigers in 2002.<ref name="ref1"/> In the same year, Yi Jianlian attended the [[Adidas]] ABCD camp in New Jersey.<ref name="ref2"/>

He first gained worldwide recognition when he was featured in [[TIME Magazine]]'s August 
24, 2003 article titled, "The Next [[Yao Ming]]." 

He won the Rookie of the Year award in the [[CBA 2002-03|2002-03 CBA season]], and won three championships with Guangdong.<ref name="ref3">{{cite web
  | last =
  | first =
  | authorlink =
  | coauthors =
  | title = 2006 FIBA World Championships
  | work =
  | publisher =
  | date =
  | url = http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/teamPlay/play/p/competitioncode//eventid/3507/langlc/en/playernumber/44281/roundid/3507/season/0/teamnumber/262/fe_teamPlay_playProf.html
  | format =
  | doi =
  | accessdate = 2007-05-25 }}</ref> In February of 2005, Yi shot 16 of 16 from the field, scoring 34 points.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= 
  | last=  
  | author=
  | url= http://english.people.com.cn/200502/03/eng20050203_172760.html 
  | title= Liaoning ensure division-leading place in CBA league
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[February 3]], [[2005]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-25
}}</ref> In what was probably Yi's last year in the CBA, the Tigers lost to the [[Bayi Rockets]] in the [[CBA 2006-07|2007 CBA]] finals, failing to win their fourth straight title.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= 
  | last=  
  | author=
  | url= http://www.china.org.cn/english/sports/205296.htm
  | title= Bayi Win Chinese Basketball Title over Guangdong
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[March 29]], [[2007]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-25
}}</ref>

Internationally, he averaged 18.9 points 11.5 rebounds a game at [[FIBA World Championship under 19|FIBA Under-19 World Championships]].<ref name="ref3"/> He debuted with the senior national team in the [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Olympic Games]], and averaged 6 points and 6 rebounds a game  at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]s,<ref name="ref3">{{cite web
  | last =
  | first =
  | authorlink =
  | coauthors =
  | title = 2006 FIBA World Championships
  | work =
  | publisher =
  | date =
  | url = http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/teamPlay/play/p/eventid/3507/langlc/en/openNodeIDs/699/playernumber/44281/roundid/3507/season/0/selNodeID/699/teamnumber/262/fe_teamPlay_playStat.html
  | format =
  | doi =
  | accessdate = 2007-05-25 }}</ref> impressing coaches on both the Chinese national team as well as the coaches from other countries.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= 
  | last= 
  | author=
  | url= http://usabasketball.com/seniormen/2006/06_mwc_exhibition_game2_quotes.html
  | title= USA-China Post Game Quotes (August 7, 2006)
  | work=
  | publisher= USA Basketball
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[August 7]], [[2006]]
  | accessdate= 2006-09-07
}}</ref>

===NBA Draft===
Yi was not expected to enter the NBA Draft until 2009 because the Chinese Basketball Association does not allow players to leave until they turn 22.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Zhau
  | last= Rui
  | author=
  | url= http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/sports/2006-11/03/content_723586.htm
  | title= Yi can enter 2007 NBA draft
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[November 3]], [[2006]]
  | accessdate= 2007-03-02
}}</ref> In early 2006, he announced he would enter the 2006 NBA Draft, although he eventually decided to withdraw, saying he was "not good enough to compete in the NBA and needed more experience."<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Zhau
  | last= Rui
  | author=
  | url= http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2006-04/20/content_4451142.htm
  | title= China's Yi Jianlian not ready for NBA yet
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[April 20]], [[2006]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-25}}</ref> However, on November 1st, 2006, Yi's club, the Guangdong Tigers, announced that Yi would enter the [[2007 NBA Draft]]. He is generally expected to be a [[NBA Lottery|lottery]] pick, as several draft sites list him in the top 10 of their [[mock draft]]s.  It was reported in China that Yi only wants to play for the [[Chicago Bulls]] or the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web

==Age discrepancy==
Questions surround his real birthdate, as his official [[passport]] and [[hukou]] in China have
him listed as being born on October 27, 1987. However, it has been rumored that his date of birth may have been intentionally falsified so he could play in junior competitions. The estimates of  his birth year are between 1984 and 1987.
In 2004, he was listed as being born in 1984 in China's Four Nation Tournament,<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Aran
  | last= Smith
  | author=
  | url= http://www.nbadraft.net/jianlianstory001.asp
  | title= Yi Jianlian actually 19 years old
  | work=
  | publisher= 
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[July 14]], [[2004]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-02
}}</ref> although authorities said it was only a “typo”. NBA draft site DraftExpress.com also listed him as being born in 1984.<ref>{{cite web
  | last =
  | first =
  | authorlink =
  | coauthors =
  | title = DraftExpress Profile : Yi Jianlian
  | work =
  | publisher =
  | date =
  | url =  http://www.draftexpress.com/viewprofile.php?p=44
  | format =
  | doi =
  | accessdate = 2007-05-25}}</ref>

The [[Houston Chronicle]]'s Fran Blinebury reported that Yi told [[Shane Battier]] he was 24
in an exhibition game before the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]].<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Fran
  | last= Blinebury
  | author=
  | url= http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/headline/sports/4142625.html
  | title= China rushing to match talent on court before 2008 Olympics
  | work=
  | publisher= [[Houston Chronicle]]
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[August 26]], [[2006]]
  | accessdate= 2007-03-12
}}</ref> However, a Chinese newspaper reported that Battier disavowed the comment attributed to him. {{Fact|date=June 2007}}Yi has gone on record saying that he did not talk to Battier about his age and that he was born in 1987 and that anyone saying anything else would be [[slander]]ing him.{{Fact|date=June 2007}}

==Personal==
Yi is fluent in both [[Standard Mandarin|Mandarin]] and his home language of [[Standard Cantonese|Cantonese]]. He also takes daily [[English language|English]] classes, and now does interviews and conversations in English without an interpreter.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Ford
  | last= Chad
  | author= Chad Ford
  | url= http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft2007/insider/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=Yi&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fnba%2fdraft2007%2finsider%2fcolumns%2fstory%3fcolumnist%3dford_chad%26page%3dYi
  | title= China rushing to match talent on court before 2008 Olympics
  | work=
  | publisher= [[ESPN]]
  | pages=
  | page=
  | date= [[May 21]], [[2007]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-25
}}</ref> 

He is currently under contract with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] to advertise their products within China.<ref>{{cite news
  | first= Matthew
  | last=  Forney
  | author=
  | url= http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,725113-4,00.html

  | work=
  | publisher=

  | date= [[October 17]], [[2004]]
  | accessdate= 2007-05-02
}}</ref>
